title: Activation Outliers Matter: Robust Recovery for Quantized Multimodal LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.26581v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Low-bit quantization offers a promising avenue for reducing the computational and memory demands of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Recent hardware support for low-precision formats, ranging from MXFP8 to ultra-low-bit formats such as MXFP4 and HiF4, has accelerated research into efficient MLLM training and deployment. In this work, we present a systematic study of these quantization schemes in representative MLLMs that span both video generation and reasoning tasks. Our analysis shows that MXFP8 achieves near-lossless performance, whereas aggressive 4-bit quantization leads to significant degradation. Through extensive ablations, we identify activation quantization as the primary source of this performance loss, contributing substantially more than weight quantization. translated_title: 激活值异常值至关重要：量化多模态大语言模型的鲁棒恢复
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26581v1 公告类型：新 摘要：低比特量化为减少多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的计算和内存需求提供了一条有前景的途径。近期硬件对低精度格式的支持，从MXFP8到MXFP4和HiF4等超低比特格式，加速了高效MLLM训练和部署的研究。在本工作中，我们对这些量化方案在代表性MLLMs中进行了系统研究，涵盖了视频生成和推理任务。我们的分析表明，MXFP8实现了接近无损的性能，而激进的4比特量化导致显著性能下降。通过广泛的消融实验，我们确定激活值量化是性能损失的主要来源，其贡献远大于权重量化。受此观察启发，我们提出了残差回退量化（RFQ），一种轻量级的激活值重建框架，用于补充主量化过程。
tldr: 本文发现激活值量化是导致多模态大语言模型在低比特量化中性能下降的主要因素，并提出残差回退量化（RFQ）框架来有效恢复性能。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies activation quantization as the primary cause of performance degradation in low-bit quantized multimodal LLMs and proposes a Residual Fallback Quantization (RFQ) framework to robustly recover performance.
